title: To and from
intro: [Unit 5](a1-u05) gave you the locative, for where things **are**. This unit adds the two cases of movement: the dative `-(y)A` for where you go (*eve*, home) and the ablative `-DAn` for where you come from (*evden*, from home). You'll also meet the irregular *bana* and *sana*, and see why a buffer *y* appears in *arabaya* but never in *arabadan*.

blocks.text: The dative (*yönelme hâli*) marks the goal of a movement: where someone goes, comes or turns. It is `-(y)A`: two-way harmony, *-e* or *-a*, with a buffer *y* after a vowel (see the last section). It has no d, so assimilation never touches it.
Names keep their apostrophe, as with the locative of [unit 5](gp-apostrophe): *Ankara'ya*, *İzmir'e*, *Paris'e*. The question word is *nereye* (where to), built on the same stem as *nerede*.

items.en: Are you coming to the cinema this evening?

blocks.text: French uses à for both place and direction: je suis à Paris, je vais à Paris. Turkish keeps them apart: *Paris'teyim* (locative), *Paris'e gidiyorum* (dative).
**Verbs that take the dative.** Some verbs put their object in the dative where English uses a direct object or another preposition. Learn them together with their case:
*Başlamak* also works without an object, like English **begin**: *Ders başlıyor* (The lesson is starting). With an object, the object goes in the dative: *Derse başlıyoruz*.
English **help Ayşe** and **believe Ali** have a direct object, but Turkish puts the person in the dative: *Ayşe'ye yardım ediyorum*, *Ali'ye inanıyorum*.

Some nouns change before the dative: *kitap* → *kitaba*, *mutfak* → *mutfağa*, *şehir* → *şehre*. [Unit 8](gp-consonant-softening) and [unit 9](gp-vowel-loss) explain these changes; until then, the exercises use words that don't change.

The ablative (*ayrılma hâli*) marks where a movement starts: **from** or **out of**. It is `-DAn`: like the locative, its vowel follows two-way harmony and its d becomes t after the voiceless consonants of *fıstıkçı şahap* ([unit 5](gp-consonant-assimilation)).

lines: -DAn → -tan / -ten   after f, s, t, k, ç, ş, h, p

blocks.text: The ablative starts with a consonant, so it never needs a buffer and never changes the stem: *arabadan*, *mutfaktan*, *kitaptan*. The question word is *nereden* (where from).

items.en: Ece is coming back from France.

blocks.text: *Nereden geliyorsun?* can also ask where someone is from, their town or country, though *Nerelisin?* from [unit 3](a1-u03) is the more usual question for that.

**Pairs of verbs.** Some movement verbs come in pairs, one with each case: *binmek* (get on) takes the dative and *inmek* (get off) the ablative, *girmek* (go in) the dative and *çıkmak* (go out) the ablative: *otobüse biniyorum* (I get on the bus), *otobüsten iniyorum* (I get off the bus); *odaya giriyorum* (I go into the room), *odadan çıkıyorum* (I come out of the room).
**Verbs of feeling.** Fear, liking and hate take the ablative: what you feel it **from**.

**From … to.** Put the start in the ablative and the end in the dative, often followed by *kadar* (as far as, until): *sabahtan akşama kadar* (from morning till evening), *evden okula kadar* (all the way from home to school).

items.en: I work from morning till evening.
We walk all the way from home to school.

blocks.text: *Neden* (why), from [unit 4](gp-question-words), is simply *ne* + `-DAn`: literally **from what**.

sections.title: Bana, sana, ondan: pronouns and place words

blocks.text: The personal pronouns take both cases. Only two forms are irregular: in the dative, *ben* and *sen* change their vowel and become *bana* and *sana*.

rows.en: to him, to her, to it
from him, from her, from it

blocks.text: *O* adds the n you know from *onda* ([unit 5](gp-pronoun-n)), and so do *bu* and *şu*: *buna*, *şuna*, *bundan*, *şundan*. Their plurals don't: *bunlara*, *onlardan*.
The place words of [unit 5](gp-pronoun-n) take the same endings as nouns, so each has three forms: where, where to and where from.

The question words work the same way: *kim* → *kime* (to whom), *kimden* (from whom); *ne* → *neye* (to what, at what): *Kime bakıyorsun?* (Who are you looking at?), *Kimden korkuyorsun?* (Who are you afraid of?), *Neye bakıyorsun?* (What are you looking at?)
Never *bene* or *sene*: in the dative the e becomes a, *bana* and *sana*. The ablative is regular: *benden*, *senden*.

Two case endings begin with a vowel: the dative `-(y)A` and the accusative `-(y)I` of [unit 8](gp-accusative). After a word that ends in a vowel, they take the buffer *y* you know from *öğrenciyim* ([unit 3](gp-buffer-letters)): *araba* + `-A` → *arabaya*. After a consonant, nothing comes between: *eve*, *okula*.

The locative `-DA` and the ablative `-DAn` begin with a consonant, so they never need a buffer: *arabada*, *arabadan*. Neither does a word that already ends in a consonant, such as a plural: *arabalara* (to the cars).

items.en: They're coming out of the museum.

blocks.text: The pronouns *o*, *bu* and *şu* take n, not y: *ona*, *buna*, *şuna*, never *oya*. And *su* (water) and *ne* (what) take y like nouns: *suya*, *neye*.

summary: The dative `-(y)A` says where to: *eve*, *okula*, *Ankara'ya*. The ablative `-DAn` says where from: *evden*, *parktan*, *Fransa'dan*.
`-DAn` becomes *-tan* or *-ten* after f, s, t, k, ç, ş, h, p. The dative starts with a vowel, so it has no such change.
*Bakmak, binmek, başlamak, inanmak* and *yardım etmek* take the dative; *korkmak, hoşlanmak* and *nefret etmek* take the ablative.
From … to: ablative, then dative, often with *kadar*: *sabahtan akşama kadar*.
*Ben* and *sen* become *bana* and *sana*; *o*, *bu* and *şu* add n: *ona*, *bundan*. Place words: *nereye*, *nereden*, *buraya*, *buradan*.
After a vowel, the dative takes a buffer y: *arabaya*. The ablative and the locative never do: *arabadan*, *arabada*.
